title: Partner AI Customization
readerIntent: Configure AI for a customer application without modifying Nodics core.
priorKnowledge: Know the application, users, data, tools, risk, providers, and budget.
owner: Customer project modules and configuration layered over reusable AI contracts
summary: Partners customize provider profiles, prompts, corpora, tools, policies, budgets, workflows, content, and branding through explicit modules and configuration.

sections.heading: Configuration-first choices
items: Enable only required AI modules and provider adapters.
Define usage profiles, allowed models, pricing, secret references, budgets, rate limits, fallback, and kill switches.
Contribute application-owned knowledge sources and classification/locale/audience policy.
Create versioned approved prompts and Assistant definitions.
Allowlist read tools and confirmation/workflow-governed mutations.
Configure retention, redaction, citations, observability, and business-facing content.

sections.heading: Application examples
items: Axis operational assistant for employee business data and actions.
Nodics documentation assistant using published documentation corpus.
Logistics assistant using that project's schemas, APIs, workflows, and guides.
Commerce support assistant using permission-safe Product, Price, Stock, order, and content contracts.
Customer support chatbot in a separate deployment and audience from an employee BackOffice assistant.

sections.heading: Deployment and extension
items: Each customer project has its own Axis/assistant deployment and effective configuration.
Tenant and project data never mix through shared conversations, corpora, ledgers, caches, or search records.
Add providers and source adapters behind provider-neutral contracts; never import vendor SDKs into callers.
Frontend owns responsive rendering and localized labels; backend owns content definitions, orchestration, security, usage, tools, and business rules.
